ball.title: Ball valves
ball.desc: Ball valves for on/off isolation. Typical applications and details needed for a quote.
ball.lead: Quarter-turn valves used for on/off isolation of a line.
apps: Isolation on process and utility lines
Fuel, oil and chemical lines, where the materials suit the medium
Isolation on pump skids and packaged equipment
consider: Full bore or reduced bore
Floating or trunnion design, which usually follows size and pressure class
Body and seat materials for the medium and temperature
Pressure class (PN or Class) and temperature range
Connection type and standard: flanged, threaded or welded
Manual, gear or actuated operation, and the actuator mounting needed
Special requirements such as fire-safe design or cleaning for the service, if your specification asks for them
ball.how: A ball valve closes with a drilled ball that turns a quarter turn inside the body. With the bore lined up with the pipe, the medium passes straight through. Turned 90 degrees, the solid side of the ball blocks the line. Ball valves are mainly used for on/off isolation rather than throttling.
variants: Floating ball
The ball is held by the seats and moves slightly under line pressure to seal. Common in smaller sizes and moderate pressure classes.
Trunnion-mounted ball
The ball is supported by a trunnion top and bottom, which lowers operating torque. Commonly used for larger sizes and higher pressure classes.
Full bore and reduced bore
Full bore matches the pipe diameter and keeps pressure loss low. Reduced bore is smaller and more compact.
Body construction
One-piece, two-piece or three-piece bodies. This affects how the valve is assembled, serviced and welded in.
End connections
Flanged, threaded, welded or socket ends, depending on the line and the standard in use.
ball.standards: Often referenced for ball valves: API 6D, API 608, ISO 17292, ASME B16.34 ratings, ISO 5211 actuator mounting, and EN 1092 or ASME B16.5 flanges.

butterfly.title: Butterfly valves
butterfly.desc: Butterfly valves for larger-diameter lines. Typical applications and details needed for a quote.
butterfly.lead: Quarter-turn valves with a disc in the flow path, commonly used on larger-diameter lines.
apps: Cooling circuits in power and process plants
Bulk powder and granule handling, in suitable designs
Flow isolation and throttling where suited
consider: Concentric, double offset or triple offset design
Wafer, lug or flanged body
Seat and disc materials for the medium
Operating and differential pressure, and temperature
Shut-off tightness required, for example a leakage class
Dead-end service, which needs a suitable lug or flanged design
Face-to-face length and flange drilling to match the existing line
Manual, gear or actuated operation, and the actuator mounting needed
butterfly.how: A disc on a stem sits in the middle of the flow path and turns a quarter turn. Parallel to the flow, the valve is open. Across the flow, it is closed. The body is short and light compared with other valve types of the same diameter, which is why butterfly valves are common on larger lines.
variants: Concentric (resilient seated)
The stem runs through the centre of the disc and an elastomer liner seals the disc. Commonly used for water, HVAC and other low-pressure, moderate-temperature service.
Double offset (high performance)
The stem is offset from the disc centre and from the seat plane, so the disc lifts away from the seat as it opens. Less seat wear and a higher pressure and temperature range than concentric.
Triple offset
A third offset in the seat geometry gives a metal-to-metal seal with almost no rubbing. Used for demanding temperature, pressure or fire-safe service.
Wafer, lug and flanged bodies
Wafer sits between two flanges. Lug has threaded lugs for bolting and can allow dead-end service where designed for it. Flanged has its own flanges.
butterfly.standards: Often referenced for butterfly valves: API 609, EN 593, ISO 5752 or EN 558 face-to-face lengths, EN 1092 or ASME B16.5 flanges, and ISO 5211 actuator mounting.

gate.title: Gate valves
gate.desc: Gate valves for straight-through isolation. Typical applications and details needed for a quote.
gate.lead: Linear-motion valves used for straight-through flow isolation, normally fully open or fully closed.
apps: Process and refinery lines, subject to technical review
Wastewater and slurry lines, using knife gate designs
consider: Rising or non-rising stem, and the headroom available
Wedge type and seat type
Body, wedge and trim materials for the medium
Pressure class (PN or Class) and temperature range
Bonnet type
End connections and the flange standard
Face-to-face length to match the existing line
Operation: handwheel, gear or actuated
gate.how: A gate or wedge moves up and down across the flow, driven by a stem. Fully raised, the flow passes through an unobstructed opening. Fully lowered, the gate seals the line. Gate valves are meant to be fully open or fully closed and are not normally used to regulate flow.
variants: Rising stem (OS&Y)
The stem rises with the gate, so the stem position shows whether the valve is open or closed. Needs headroom above the valve.
Non-rising stem
The stem turns in the gate without moving up. Lower overall height, so it suits tight spaces and buried installations.
Wedge designs
Solid, flexible or split wedge. The choice affects sealing, thermal behaviour and suitability for the medium.
Resilient seated and metal seated
Resilient seats are common on water. Metal seats are common on steam, oil and higher temperatures.
Bonnet and body
Bolted, pressure-seal or welded bonnets. Cast iron, ductile iron, cast steel, stainless steel and bronze bodies, depending on the service.
Knife gate
A thin blade cuts through thick media such as slurries and pulp. Related to gate valves but a different design.
gate.standards: Often referenced for gate valves: API 600, API 602, EN 1171, DIN 3352, ASME B16.34 ratings, ASME B16.10 or EN 558 face-to-face lengths, and EN 1092 or ASME B16.5 flanges.

check.title: Check valves
check.desc: Check valves to prevent backflow. Typical applications and details needed for a quote.
check.lead: Valves that allow flow in one direction and prevent backflow.
apps: Sewage and sludge lines, using suitable designs
consider: Swing, dual-plate, lift or axial design
Installation orientation and the direction of flow
Minimum flow needed to open the valve fully
Opening pressure and spring requirements
Closing behaviour, including water hammer risk on pump lines
Body and seal materials for the medium
Pressure rating and temperature range
Connection type: wafer, flanged or threaded
check.how: A check valve opens by itself when the medium flows forward and closes when the flow reverses. It needs no handwheel or actuator. The disc, plate or ball is moved by the flow, and often assisted by a spring or by gravity.
variants: Swing check
A hinged disc swings open with the flow. Low pressure loss. Usually installed horizontally, or vertically with upward flow.
Dual-plate (wafer) check
Two spring-loaded half plates between flanges. Compact and light, and fast to close.
Lift check
A disc or piston lifts off its seat, guided by the body. Used on higher pressures and steam. Installed in the orientation the design allows.
Axial (nozzle) check
A spring-assisted disc on the flow axis with a short closing stroke. Used where slam on closure is a concern.
Ball check
A ball moves in a cage. Simple, and suited to viscous or dirty media in the right design.
check.standards: Often referenced for check valves: API 594, API 6D, BS 1868, EN 12334, EN 558 face-to-face lengths, ASME B16.34 ratings, and EN 1092 or ASME B16.5 flanges.

technical.title: Technical Supply
technical.desc: Which application and valve details help us assess a request. A technical enquiry guide.
technical.lead: A valve is chosen for an application, not from a product description alone. This guide shows which details help us assess your request. It does not replace engineering approval.
guide_rows: Ball, butterfly, gate or check. If unsure, describe what the valve must do.
Nominal diameter, for example DN50 or 2 inch.
Pieces required, and whether this is a one-off or repeat need.
What flows through the valve: water, oil, gas, chemical, solids.
Working and design pressure, and any pressure class required.
Body, seat and trim materials, or the medium so we can discuss options.
Flanged, threaded, wafer, lug or welded, with standard if known.
Applicable standards, datasheets, drawings, certificates required.
Destination and the date you need the valves.
technical.notes_p: We check your details for completeness, ask for what is missing, and confirm that a credible supply option exists. Documents are reviewed against the actual product before any offer.
technical.limits_p: It does not provide automatic technical recommendations or engineering approval. Suitability is confirmed against your actual application and requirements.
technical.nodata_p: Describe what the valve must do, where it sits in the line, and what flows through it. Add a photo of the old valve or its nameplate if you are replacing one. We ask follow-up questions for anything missing.
terms_rows: Nominal diameter in millimetres, for example DN100.
Nominal pressure rating in bar for European flanges, for example PN16.
Pressure class on the ASME scale, for example Class 150 or 300.
Length of the valve body between its connection faces. It must match the line.
The flow opening. Full bore equals the pipe diameter, reduced bore is smaller.
Body styles for fitting between or onto pipe flanges.
The sealing surface. Soft (elastomer or polymer) or metal.
Operated by a pneumatic, electric or hydraulic actuator instead of a handwheel or lever.
checklist: The valve type, or what it must do if you are not sure
The medium, with working pressure and temperature
Connection type and flange standard, if known
Any standards, datasheet or drawing that apply
Destination country and the date you need the valves
technical.disclaimer: Terms are explained in general. They do not replace engineering approval for your application.

process.title: How Sourcing Works
process.desc: From requirement review to supply coordination. What happens after you send an enquiry.
process.lead: One enquiry, with a person reviewing at each stage. This is what happens after you submit, from your side.
steps: Fill in the form. Five fields are required: your name, company, email, country and what you need. Technical details and files are optional, and you can submit with incomplete information.

Once your enquiry is stored, the page shows a reference number and a confirmation email goes to the address you gave. If sending fails, your details stay in the form so you can retry without retyping.
A person reads your enquiry and checks technical completeness. If something is missing, we write to you with specific questions. You do not need to chase.
We confirm whether a credible supply option exists for your requirement, and check documents against the actual product.
Specifications, terms and delivery assumptions are reviewed by a person before an offer is sent to you.
We send an offer, or tell you plainly if we cannot meet the requirement or need more information first.
We follow up on the offer. If you go ahead, we coordinate the process toward delivery and keep you informed.
process.note: No quotation is sent without human review. Timing depends on the request and is not promised on this site.
who: You contact us once, through the form. You do not need to send several emails to start. [pending approval]
After that, we contact you, normally by email at the address you gave. Tell us in the form if you prefer a phone call. [pending approval]
If a question comes up, reply to the confirmation email and quote your reference.
We do not contact third parties about your enquiry without telling you. [pending approval]
process.after_p: The confirmation tells you that your enquiry was received and stored. It is not an offer, a price or a commitment to supply. A quotation follows only after review. [pending approval]
